# Resource: stripe_invoice

A bill for a customer. With `pending_invoice_items_behavior = "include"` it takes the customer's pending invoice items when it is created. `terraform destroy` deletes a draft invoice, and Stripe deletes the invoice items on it too. Set `status` to `open` to finalize a draft, to `paid` to finalize it if need be and charge its `default_payment_method`, to `void` to void an open or uncollectible invoice, or to `uncollectible` to mark an open one uncollectible. With `auto_advance`, Stripe finalizes a draft and collects payment by itself. Once an invoice is finalized Stripe refuses changes to most arguments, but `metadata` still changes. Finalizing turns a `rendering.pdf.page_size` of `auto` into the page size Stripe picks, such as `letter`, so set `a4` or `letter` on an invoice you finalize, or leave `rendering` unset. The invoice's `last_finalization_error` is not available.

~> An invoice can move real money. In a live-mode Stripe account, creating or changing one, including setting its `status`, fails at plan time unless the provider sets `allow_live_money_movement = true`. Reading or importing one never does. The provider asks Stripe for the account's mode. See the Managing Test Data guide.

~> Stripe deletes only a draft invoice; a finalized one stays in the account. `terraform destroy`, and a change that would replace it, fail at plan time for such an invoice. To stop managing one, remove it from the state as [Removing from State](#removing-from-state) shows; it stays in the Stripe account.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "stripe_customer" "acme" {
  email = "billing@acme.example"
}

# A pending item, which the invoice sweeps up when it is created.
resource "stripe_invoiceitem" "setup_fee" {
  customer    = stripe_customer.acme.id
  amount      = 5000
  currency    = "usd"
  description = "One-time setup fee"
}

# Finalized and left open for the customer to pay from the emailed invoice.
resource "stripe_invoice" "setup" {
  customer                       = stripe_customer.acme.id
  currency                       = "usd"
  collection_method              = "send_invoice"
  days_until_due                 = 30
  auto_advance                   = false
  pending_invoice_items_behavior = "include"
  status                         = "open"

  depends_on = [stripe_invoiceitem.setup_fee]
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are optional:

* `account_tax_ids` - (Optional) The account tax IDs associated with the invoice. Only editable when the invoice is a draft. Changing it replaces the resource.
* `application_fee_amount` - (Optional) A fee in cents (or local equivalent) that will be applied to the invoice and transferred to the application owner's Stripe account. The request must be made with an OAuth key or the Stripe-Account header in order to take an application fee. For more information, see the application fees [documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/invoices/connect#collecting-fees). Changing it replaces the resource.
* `auto_advance` - (Optional) Controls whether Stripe performs [automatic collection](https://docs.stripe.com/invoicing/integration/automatic-advancement-collection) of the invoice. If `false`, the invoice's state doesn't automatically advance without an explicit action. Defaults to false. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `automatic_tax` - (Optional) Settings for automatic tax lookup for this invoice. Changing it replaces the resource. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`automatic_tax`](#automatic_tax) below.
* `automatically_finalizes_at` - (Optional) The time when this invoice should be scheduled to finalize (up to 5 years in the future). The invoice is finalized at this time if it's still in draft state. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `collection_method` - (Optional) Either `charge_automatically`, or `send_invoice`. When charging automatically, Stripe will attempt to pay this invoice using the default source attached to the customer. When sending an invoice, Stripe will email this invoice to the customer with payment instructions. Defaults to `charge_automatically`. Possible values: `charge_automatically`, `send_invoice`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `currency` - (Optional) The currency to create this invoice in. Defaults to that of `customer` if not specified. Changing it replaces the resource. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `custom_fields` - (Optional) A list of up to 4 custom fields to be displayed on the invoice. See [`custom_fields`](#custom_fields) below.
* `customer` - (Optional) The ID of the customer to bill. Changing it replaces the resource. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `customer_account` - (Optional) The ID of the account to bill. Changing it replaces the resource.
* `days_until_due` - (Optional) The number of days from when the invoice is created until it is due. Valid only for invoices where `collection_method=send_invoice`.
* `default_payment_method` - (Optional) ID of the default payment method for the invoice. It must belong to the customer associated with the invoice. If not set, defaults to the subscription's default payment method, if any, or to the default payment method in the customer's invoice settings.
* `default_source` - (Optional) ID of the default payment source for the invoice. It must belong to the customer associated with the invoice and be in a chargeable state. If not set, defaults to the subscription's default source, if any, or to the customer's default source. Changing it replaces the resource.
* `default_tax_rates` - (Optional) The tax rates that will apply to any line item that does not have `tax_rates` set. Changing it replaces the resource. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `description` - (Optional) An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users. Referenced as 'memo' in the Dashboard.
* `due_date` - (Optional) The date on which payment for this invoice is due. Valid only for invoices where `collection_method=send_invoice`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `effective_at` - (Optional) The date when this invoice is in effect. Same as `finalized_at` unless overwritten. When defined, this value replaces the system-generated 'Date of issue' printed on the invoice PDF and receipt. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `footer` - (Optional) Footer to be displayed on the invoice.
* `from_invoice` - (Optional) Revise an existing invoice. The new invoice will be created in `status=draft`. See the [revision documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/invoicing/invoice-revisions) for more details. Changing it replaces the resource. See [`from_invoice`](#from_invoice) below.
* `issuer` - (Optional) The connected account that issues the invoice. The invoice is presented with the branding and support information of the specified account. Changing it replaces the resource. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`issuer`](#issuer) below.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.
* `number` - (Optional) Set the number for this invoice. If no number is present then a number will be assigned automatically when the invoice is finalized. In many markets, regulations require invoices to be unique, sequential and / or gapless. You are responsible for ensuring this is true across all your different invoicing systems in the event that you edit the invoice number using our API. If you use only Stripe for your invoices and do not change invoice numbers, Stripe handles this aspect of compliance for you automatically. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `on_behalf_of` - (Optional) The account (if any) for which the funds of the invoice payment are intended. If set, the invoice will be presented with the branding and support information of the specified account. See the [Invoices with Connect](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/invoices/connect) documentation for details. Changing it replaces the resource.
* `payment_settings` - (Optional) Configuration settings for the PaymentIntent that is generated when the invoice is finalized. Changing it replaces the resource. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`payment_settings`](#payment_settings) below.
* `pending_invoice_items_behavior` - (Optional) How to handle pending invoice items on invoice creation. Defaults to `exclude` if the parameter is omitted. Possible values: `exclude`, `include`. Changing it replaces the resource.
* `rendering` - (Optional) The rendering-related settings that control how invoices render in customer-facing interfaces such as the PDF or hosted invoice page. Changing it replaces the resource. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`rendering`](#rendering) below.
* `shipping_cost` - (Optional) Settings for the cost of shipping for this invoice. Changing it replaces the resource. See [`shipping_cost`](#shipping_cost) below.
* `shipping_details` - (Optional) Shipping details for the invoice. The Invoice PDF will use the `shipping_details` value if it is set, otherwise the PDF will render the shipping address from the customer. Changing it replaces the resource. See [`shipping_details`](#shipping_details) below.
* `statement_descriptor` - (Optional) Extra information about a charge for the customer's credit card statement. It must contain at least one letter. If not specified and this invoice is part of a subscription, the default `statement_descriptor` will be set to the first subscription item's product's `statement_descriptor`.
* `status` - (Optional) The status of the invoice, one of `draft`, `open`, `paid`, `uncollectible`, or `void`. [Learn more](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/invoices/workflow#workflow-overview) Possible values: `open`, `paid`, `void`, `uncollectible`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `subscription` - (Optional) The ID of the subscription to invoice, if any. If set, the created invoice will only include pending invoice items for that subscription. The subscription's billing cycle and regular subscription events won't be affected. Changing it replaces the resource.
* `transfer_data` - (Optional) If specified, the funds from the invoice will be transferred to the destination and the ID of the resulting transfer will be found on the invoice's charge. Changing it replaces the resource. See [`transfer_data`](#transfer_data) below.

<a id="automatic_tax"></a>
### `automatic_tax`

The `automatic_tax` attribute supports:

* `disabled_reason` - (Read-Only) If Stripe disabled automatic tax, this enum describes why. Possible values: `finalization_requires_location_inputs`, `finalization_system_error`.
* `enabled` - (Required) Whether Stripe automatically computes tax on this invoice. Note that incompatible invoice items (invoice items with manually specified [tax rates](https://docs.stripe.com/api/tax_rates), negative amounts, or `tax_behavior=unspecified`) cannot be added to automatic tax invoices.
* `liability` - (Optional) The account that's liable for tax. If set, the business address and tax registrations required to perform the tax calculation are loaded from this account. The tax transaction is returned in the report of the connected account. See [`automatic_tax.liability`](#automatic_tax.liability) below.
* `provider` - (Read-Only) The tax provider powering automatic tax.
* `status` - (Read-Only) The status of the most recent automated tax calculation for this invoice. Possible values: `complete`, `failed`, `requires_location_inputs`.

<a id="automatic_tax.liability"></a>
### `automatic_tax.liability`

The `automatic_tax.liability` attribute supports:

* `account` - (Optional) The connected account being referenced when `type` is `account`.
* `type` - (Required) Type of the account referenced. Possible values: `account`, `self`.

<a id="custom_fields"></a>
### `custom_fields`

The `custom_fields` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `name` - (Required) The name of the custom field.
* `value` - (Required) The value of the custom field.

<a id="from_invoice"></a>
### `from_invoice`

The `from_invoice` attribute supports:

* `action` - (Required) The relation between this invoice and the cloned invoice Possible values: `revision`.
* `invoice` - (Required) The invoice that was cloned.

<a id="issuer"></a>
### `issuer`

The `issuer` attribute supports:

* `account` - (Optional) The connected account being referenced when `type` is `account`.
* `type` - (Required) Type of the account referenced. Possible values: `account`, `self`.

<a id="payment_settings"></a>
### `payment_settings`

The `payment_settings` attribute supports:

* `default_mandate` - (Optional) ID of the mandate to be used for this invoice. It must correspond to the payment method used to pay the invoice, including the invoice's default_payment_method or default_source, if set.
* `payment_method_options` - (Optional) Payment-method-specific configuration to provide to the invoice’s PaymentIntent. See [`payment_settings.payment_method_options`](#payment_settings.payment_method_options) below.
* `payment_method_types` - (Optional) The list of payment method types (e.g. card) to provide to the invoice’s PaymentIntent. If not set, Stripe attempts to automatically determine the types to use by looking at the invoice’s default payment method, the subscription’s default payment method, the customer’s default payment method, and your [invoice template settings](https://dashboard.stripe.com/settings/billing/invoice).

<a id="payment_settings.payment_method_options"></a>
### `payment_settings.payment_method_options`

The `payment_settings.payment_method_options` attribute supports:

* `acss_debit` - (Optional) If paying by `acss_debit`, this sub-hash contains details about the Canadian pre-authorized debit payment method options to pass to the invoice’s PaymentIntent. See [`payment_settings.payment_method_options.acss_debit`](#payment_settings.payment_method_options.acss_debit) below.
* `bancontact` - (Optional) If paying by `bancontact`, this sub-hash contains details about the Bancontact payment method options to pass to the invoice’s PaymentIntent. See [`payment_settings.payment_method_options.bancontact`](#payment_settings.payment_method_options.bancontact) below.
* `billie` - (Optional) If paying by `billie`, this sub-hash contains details about the Billie payment method options to pass to the invoice’s PaymentIntent. See [`payment_settings.payment_method_options.billie`](#payment_settings.payment_method_options.billie) below.
* `card` - (Optional) If paying by `card`, this sub-hash contains details about the Card payment method options to pass to the invoice’s PaymentIntent. See [`payment_settings.payment_method_options.card`](#payment_settings.payment_method_options.card) below.
* `customer_balance` - (Optional) If paying by `customer_balance`, this sub-hash contains details about the Bank transfer payment method options to pass to the invoice’s PaymentIntent. See [`payment_settings.payment_method_options.customer_balance`](#payment_settings.payment_method_options.customer_balance) below.
* `payto` - (Optional) If paying by `payto`, this sub-hash contains details about the PayTo payment method options to pass to the invoice’s PaymentIntent. See [`payment_settings.payment_method_options.payto`](#payment_settings.payment_method_options.payto) below.
* `pix` - (Optional) If paying by `pix`, this sub-hash contains details about the Pix payment method options to pass to the invoice’s PaymentIntent. See [`payment_settings.payment_method_options.pix`](#payment_settings.payment_method_options.pix) below.
* `upi` - (Optional) If paying by `upi`, this sub-hash contains details about the UPI payment method options to pass to the invoice’s PaymentIntent. See [`payment_settings.payment_method_options.upi`](#payment_settings.payment_method_options.upi) below.
* `us_bank_account` - (Optional) If paying by `us_bank_account`, this sub-hash contains details about the ACH direct debit payment method options to pass to the invoice’s PaymentIntent. See [`payment_settings.payment_method_options.us_bank_account`](#payment_settings.payment_method_options.us_bank_account) below.

<a id="payment_settings.payment_method_options.acss_debit"></a>
### `payment_settings.payment_method_options.acss_debit`

The `payment_settings.payment_method_options.acss_debit` attribute supports:

* `verification_method` - (Optional) Bank account verification method. The default value is `automatic`. Possible values: `automatic`, `instant`, `microdeposits`.

<a id="payment_settings.payment_method_options.acss_debit.mandate_options"></a>
### `payment_settings.payment_method_options.acss_debit.mandate_options`

The `payment_settings.payment_method_options.acss_debit.mandate_options` attribute supports:

* `transaction_type` - (Optional) Transaction type of the mandate. Possible values: `business`, `personal`.

<a id="payment_settings.payment_method_options.bancontact"></a>
### `payment_settings.payment_method_options.bancontact`

The `payment_settings.payment_method_options.bancontact` attribute supports:

<a id="payment_settings.payment_method_options.billie"></a>
### `payment_settings.payment_method_options.billie`

The `payment_settings.payment_method_options.billie` attribute supports:

* `reference` - (Optional) An identifier or reference that this payment corresponds to.

<a id="payment_settings.payment_method_options.billie.company_details"></a>
### `payment_settings.payment_method_options.billie.company_details`

The `payment_settings.payment_method_options.billie.company_details` attribute supports:

* `registered_address` - (Optional) See [`payment_settings.payment_method_options.billie.company_details.registered_address`](#payment_settings.payment_method_options.billie.company_details.registered_address) below.
* `registered_name` - (Optional) Company or entity name.
* `registration_number` - (Optional) The official registration number for the given registration type.
* `registration_type` - (Optional) Type of registration the company or entity holds in their registered country. Possible values: `ch_ein`, `de_hrb`, `dk_cvr`, `es_cif`, `fi_tunnus`, `fr_siren`, `fr_siret`, `it_rea`, `nl_kvk`, `no_org_number`, `no_pno`, `se_org_number`, `se_pno`, `uk_crn`.
* `vat` - (Optional) VAT ID number.

<a id="payment_settings.payment_method_options.billie.company_details.registered_address"></a>
### `payment_settings.payment_method_options.billie.company_details.registered_address`

The `payment_settings.payment_method_options.billie.company_details.registered_address` attribute supports:

* `city` - (Optional) City, district, suburb, town, or village.
* `country` - (Optional) Two-letter country code.
* `line1` - (Optional) Address line 1 (for example, street, PO Box, or company name).
* `line2` - (Optional) Address line 2 (for example, apartment, suite, unit, or building).
* `postal_code` - (Optional) ZIP or postal code.
* `state` - (Optional) State, county, province, or region.

<a id="payment_settings.payment_method_options.card"></a>
### `payment_settings.payment_method_options.card`

The `payment_settings.payment_method_options.card` attribute supports:

* `installments` - (Optional) See [`payment_settings.payment_method_options.card.installments`](#payment_settings.payment_method_options.card.installments) below.
* `request_three_d_secure` - (Optional) We strongly recommend that you rely on our SCA Engine to automatically prompt your customers for authentication based on risk level and [other requirements](https://docs.stripe.com/strong-customer-authentication). However, if you wish to request 3D Secure based on logic from your own fraud engine, provide this option. Read our guide on [manually requesting 3D Secure](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/3d-secure/authentication-flow#manual-three-ds) for more information on how this configuration interacts with Radar and our SCA Engine. Possible values: `any`, `automatic`, `challenge`.

<a id="payment_settings.payment_method_options.card.installments"></a>

<a id="payment_settings.payment_method_options.payto"></a>
### `payment_settings.payment_method_options.payto`

The `payment_settings.payment_method_options.payto` attribute supports:

* `mandate_options` - (Optional) See [`payment_settings.payment_method_options.payto.mandate_options`](#payment_settings.payment_method_options.payto.mandate_options) below.

<a id="payment_settings.payment_method_options.payto.mandate_options"></a>
### `payment_settings.payment_method_options.payto.mandate_options`

The `payment_settings.payment_method_options.payto.mandate_options` attribute supports:

* `amount` - (Optional) The maximum amount that can be collected in a single invoice. If you don't specify a maximum, then there is no limit.
* `amount_type` - (Read-Only) Only `maximum` is supported. Possible values: `fixed`, `maximum`.
* `purpose` - (Optional) The purpose for which payments are made. Has a default value based on your merchant category code. Possible values: `dependant_support`, `government`, `loan`, `mortgage`, `other`, `pension`, `personal`, `retail`, `salary`, `tax`, `utility`.

<a id="payment_settings.payment_method_options.pix"></a>
### `payment_settings.payment_method_options.pix`

The `payment_settings.payment_method_options.pix` attribute supports:

* `amount_includes_iof` - (Optional) Determines if the amount includes the IOF tax. Possible values: `always`, `never`.
* `expires_after_seconds` - (Optional) The number of seconds (between 10 and 1209600) after which Pix payment will expire. Defaults to 86400 seconds.

<a id="payment_settings.payment_method_options.upi"></a>
### `payment_settings.payment_method_options.upi`

The `payment_settings.payment_method_options.upi` attribute supports:

* `mandate_options` - (Optional) See [`payment_settings.payment_method_options.upi.mandate_options`](#payment_settings.payment_method_options.upi.mandate_options) below.

<a id="payment_settings.payment_method_options.upi.mandate_options"></a>
### `payment_settings.payment_method_options.upi.mandate_options`

The `payment_settings.payment_method_options.upi.mandate_options` attribute supports:

* `amount` - (Optional) Amount to be charged for future payments.
* `amount_type` - (Optional) One of `fixed` or `maximum`. If `fixed`, the `amount` param refers to the exact amount to be charged in future payments. If `maximum`, the amount charged can be up to the value passed for the `amount` param. Possible values: `fixed`, `maximum`.
* `description` - (Optional) A description of the mandate or subscription that is meant to be displayed to the customer.
* `end_date` - (Optional) End date of the mandate or subscription.

The `payment_settings.payment_method_options.us_bank_account` attribute supports:

* `verification_method` - (Optional) Bank account verification method. The default value is `automatic`. Possible values: `automatic`, `instant`, `microdeposits`.

<a id="payment_settings.payment_method_options.us_bank_account.financial_connections"></a>
### `payment_settings.payment_method_options.us_bank_account.financial_connections`

The `payment_settings.payment_method_options.us_bank_account.financial_connections` attribute supports:

<a id="rendering"></a>
### `rendering`

The `rendering` attribute supports:

* `pdf` - (Optional) Invoice pdf rendering options See [`rendering.pdf`](#rendering.pdf) below.
* `template` - (Optional) ID of the rendering template that the invoice is formatted by.
* `template_version` - (Optional) Version of the rendering template that the invoice is using.

<a id="rendering.pdf"></a>
### `rendering.pdf`

The `rendering.pdf` attribute supports:

* `page_size` - (Optional) Page size of invoice pdf. Options include a4, letter, and auto. If set to auto, page size will be switched to a4 or letter based on customer locale. Possible values: `a4`, `auto`, `letter`.

<a id="shipping_cost"></a>
### `shipping_cost`

The `shipping_cost` attribute supports:

* `amount_subtotal` - (Read-Only) Total shipping cost before any taxes are applied.
* `amount_tax` - (Read-Only) Total tax amount applied due to shipping costs. If no tax was applied, defaults to 0.
* `amount_total` - (Read-Only) Total shipping cost after taxes are applied.
* `shipping_rate` - (Optional) The ID of the ShippingRate for this invoice.
* `shipping_rate_data` - (Optional) See [`shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data`](#shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data) below.
* `taxes` - (Read-Only) The taxes applied to the shipping rate. See [`shipping_cost.taxes`](#shipping_cost.taxes) below.

<a id="shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data"></a>
### `shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data`

The `shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data` attribute supports:

* `delivery_estimate` - (Optional) See [`shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data.delivery_estimate`](#shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data.delivery_estimate) below.
* `display_name` - (Required)
* `fixed_amount` - (Optional) See [`shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data.fixed_amount`](#shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data.fixed_amount) below.
* `metadata` - (Optional)
* `tax_behavior` - (Optional) Possible values: `exclusive`, `inclusive`, `unspecified`.
* `tax_code` - (Optional)
* `type` - (Optional) Possible values: `fixed_amount`.

<a id="shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data.delivery_estimate"></a>
### `shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data.delivery_estimate`

The `shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data.delivery_estimate` attribute supports:

* `maximum` - (Optional) See [`shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data.delivery_estimate.maximum`](#shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data.delivery_estimate.maximum) below.
* `minimum` - (Optional) See [`shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data.delivery_estimate.minimum`](#shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data.delivery_estimate.minimum) below.

<a id="shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data.delivery_estimate.maximum"></a>
### `shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data.delivery_estimate.maximum`

The `shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data.delivery_estimate.maximum` attribute supports:

* `unit` - (Required) Possible values: `business_day`, `day`, `hour`, `month`, `week`.
* `value` - (Required)

<a id="shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data.delivery_estimate.minimum"></a>
### `shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data.delivery_estimate.minimum`

The `shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data.delivery_estimate.minimum` attribute supports:

* `unit` - (Required) Possible values: `business_day`, `day`, `hour`, `month`, `week`.
* `value` - (Required)

<a id="shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data.fixed_amount"></a>
### `shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data.fixed_amount`

The `shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data.fixed_amount` attribute supports:

* `amount` - (Required)
* `currency` - (Required)
* `currency_options` - (Optional) See [`shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data.fixed_amount.currency_options`](#shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data.fixed_amount.currency_options) below.

<a id="shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data.fixed_amount.currency_options"></a>
### `shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data.fixed_amount.currency_options`

The `shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data.fixed_amount.currency_options` attribute is a map. Each value supports:

* `amount` - (Required)
* `tax_behavior` - (Optional) Possible values: `exclusive`, `inclusive`, `unspecified`.

<a id="shipping_cost.taxes"></a>
### `shipping_cost.taxes`

The `shipping_cost.taxes` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - Amount of tax applied for this rate.
* `rate` - Tax rates can be applied to [invoices](https://docs.stripe.com/invoicing/taxes/tax-rates), [subscriptions](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/taxes/tax-rates) and [Checkout Sessions](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout/use-manual-tax-rates) to collect tax. Related guide: [Tax rates](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/taxes/tax-rates) See [`shipping_cost.taxes.rate`](#shipping_cost.taxes.rate) below.
* `taxability_reason` - The reasoning behind this tax, for example, if the product is tax exempt. The possible values for this field may be extended as new tax rules are supported. Possible values: `customer_exempt`, `not_collecting`, `not_subject_to_tax`, `not_supported`, `portion_product_exempt`, `portion_reduced_rated`, `portion_standard_rated`, `product_exempt`, `product_exempt_holiday`, `proportionally_rated`, `reduced_rated`, `reverse_charge`, `standard_rated`, `taxable_basis_reduced`, `zero_rated`.
* `taxable_amount` - The amount on which tax is calculated, in cents (or local equivalent).

<a id="shipping_cost.taxes.rate"></a>
### `shipping_cost.taxes.rate`

The `shipping_cost.taxes.rate` attribute holds a tax rate, with the attributes of the [`stripe_tax_rate`](../data-sources/tax_rate) data source and `object`, the name of its type.

<a id="shipping_details"></a>
### `shipping_details`

The `shipping_details` attribute supports:

* `address` - (Required) See [`shipping_details.address`](#shipping_details.address) below.
* `carrier` - (Read-Only) The delivery service that shipped a physical product, such as Fedex, UPS, USPS, etc.
* `name` - (Required) Recipient name.
* `phone` - (Optional) Recipient phone (including extension).
* `tracking_number` - (Read-Only) The tracking number for a physical product, obtained from the delivery service. If multiple tracking numbers were generated for this purchase, please separate them with commas.

<a id="shipping_details.address"></a>
### `shipping_details.address`

The `shipping_details.address` attribute supports:

* `city` - (Optional) City, district, suburb, town, or village.
* `country` - (Optional) Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).
* `line1` - (Optional) Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name.
* `line2` - (Optional) Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.
* `postal_code` - (Optional) ZIP or postal code.
* `state` - (Optional) State, county, province, or region ([ISO 3166-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2)).

<a id="transfer_data"></a>
### `transfer_data`

The `transfer_data` attribute supports:

* `amount` - (Optional)
* `destination` - (Required)

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object. For preview invoices created using the [create preview](https://stripe.com/docs/api/invoices/create_preview) endpoint, this id will be prefixed with `upcoming_in`.
* `account_country` - The country of the business associated with this invoice, most often the business creating the invoice.
* `account_name` - The public name of the business associated with this invoice, most often the business creating the invoice.
* `amount_due` - Final amount due at this time for this invoice. If the invoice's total is smaller than the minimum charge amount, for example, or if there is account credit that can be applied to the invoice, the `amount_due` may be 0. If there is a positive `starting_balance` for the invoice (the customer owes money), the `amount_due` will also take that into account. The charge that gets generated for the invoice will be for the amount specified in `amount_due`.
* `amount_overpaid` - Amount that was overpaid on the invoice. The amount overpaid is credited to the customer's credit balance.
* `amount_paid` - The amount, in cents (or local equivalent), that was paid.
* `amount_paid_off_stripe` - Amount, in cents (or local equivalent), that was paid on the invoice outside of Stripe.
* `amount_remaining` - The difference between amount_due and amount_paid, in cents (or local equivalent).
* `amount_shipping` - This is the sum of all the shipping amounts.
* `application` - ID of the Connect Application that created the invoice.
* `attempt_count` - Number of payment attempts made for this invoice, from the perspective of the payment retry schedule. Any payment attempt counts as the first attempt, and subsequently only automatic retries increment the attempt count. In other words, manual payment attempts after the first attempt do not affect the retry schedule. If a failure is returned with a non-retryable return code, the invoice can no longer be retried unless a new payment method is obtained. Retries will continue to be scheduled, and attempt_count will continue to increment, but retries will only be executed if a new payment method is obtained.
* `attempted` - Whether an attempt has been made to pay the invoice. An invoice is not attempted until 1 hour after the `invoice.created` webhook, for example, so you might not want to display that invoice as unpaid to your users.
* `billing_reason` - Indicates the reason why the invoice was created. * `manual`: Unrelated to a subscription, for example, created via the invoice editor. * `subscription`: No longer in use. Applies to subscriptions from before May 2018 where no distinction was made between updates, cycles, and thresholds. * `subscription_create`: A new subscription was created. * `subscription_cycle`: A subscription advanced into a new period. * `subscription_threshold`: A subscription reached a billing threshold. * `subscription_update`: A subscription was updated. * `upcoming`: Reserved for upcoming invoices created through the Create Preview Invoice API or when an `invoice.upcoming` event is generated for an upcoming invoice on a subscription. Possible values: `automatic_pending_invoice_item_invoice`, `manual`, `quote_accept`, `subscription`, `subscription_create`, `subscription_cycle`, `subscription_threshold`, `subscription_update`, `upcoming`.
* `confirmation_secret` - The confirmation secret associated with this invoice. Currently, this contains the client_secret of the PaymentIntent that Stripe creates during invoice finalization. See [`confirmation_secret`](#confirmation_secret) below.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `customer_address` - The customer's address. Until the invoice is finalized, this field will equal `customer.address`. Once the invoice is finalized, this field will no longer be updated. See [`customer_address`](#customer_address) below.
* `customer_email` - The customer's email. Until the invoice is finalized, this field will equal `customer.email`. Once the invoice is finalized, this field will no longer be updated.
* `customer_name` - The customer's name. Until the invoice is finalized, this field will equal `customer.name`. Once the invoice is finalized, this field will no longer be updated.
* `customer_phone` - The customer's phone number. Until the invoice is finalized, this field will equal `customer.phone`. Once the invoice is finalized, this field will no longer be updated.
* `customer_shipping` - The customer's shipping information. Until the invoice is finalized, this field will equal `customer.shipping`. Once the invoice is finalized, this field will no longer be updated. See [`customer_shipping`](#customer_shipping) below.
* `customer_tax_exempt` - The customer's tax exempt status. Until the invoice is finalized, this field will equal `customer.tax_exempt`. Once the invoice is finalized, this field will no longer be updated. Possible values: `exempt`, `none`, `reverse`.
* `customer_tax_ids` - The customer's tax IDs. Until the invoice is finalized, this field will contain the same tax IDs as `customer.tax_ids`. Once the invoice is finalized, this field will no longer be updated. See [`customer_tax_ids`](#customer_tax_ids) below.
* `ending_balance` - Ending customer balance after the invoice is finalized. Invoices are finalized approximately an hour after successful webhook delivery or when payment collection is attempted for the invoice. If the invoice has not been finalized yet, this will be null.
* `hosted_invoice_url` - The URL for the hosted invoice page, which allows customers to view and pay an invoice. If the invoice has not been finalized yet, this will be null.
* `invoice_pdf` - The link to download the PDF for the invoice. If the invoice has not been finalized yet, this will be null.
* `latest_revision` - The ID of the most recent non-draft revision of this invoice
* `lines` - The individual line items that make up the invoice. `lines` is sorted as follows: (1) pending invoice items (including prorations) in reverse chronological order, (2) subscription items in reverse chronological order, and (3) invoice items added after invoice creation in chronological order. Holds the first page of the list Stripe returns with the object; `has_more` is true when there are more. Read every element with the `stripe_invoice_line` data source. See [`lines`](#lines) below.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `next_payment_attempt` - The time at which payment will next be attempted. This value will be `null` for invoices where `collection_method=send_invoice`.
* `parent` - The parent that generated this invoice See [`parent`](#parent) below.
* `payments` - Payments for this invoice. Use [invoice payment](https://docs.stripe.com/api/invoice-payment) to get more details. See [`payments`](#payments) below.
* `period_end` - The latest timestamp at which invoice items can be associated with this invoice. Use the [line item period](https://docs.stripe.com/api/invoices/line_item#invoice_line_item_object-period) to get the service period for each price.
* `period_start` - The earliest timestamp at which invoice items can be associated with this invoice. Use the [line item period](https://docs.stripe.com/api/invoices/line_item#invoice_line_item_object-period) to get the service period for each price.
* `post_payment_credit_notes_amount` - Total amount of all post-payment credit notes issued for this invoice.
* `pre_payment_credit_notes_amount` - Total amount of all pre-payment credit notes issued for this invoice.
* `receipt_number` - This is the transaction number that appears on email receipts sent for this invoice.
* `starting_balance` - Starting customer balance before the invoice is finalized. If the invoice has not been finalized yet, this will be the current customer balance. For revision invoices, this also includes any customer balance that was applied to the original invoice.
* `status_details` - See [`status_details`](#status_details) below.
* `status_transitions` - See [`status_transitions`](#status_transitions) below.
* `subtotal` - Total of all subscriptions, invoice items, and prorations on the invoice before any invoice level discount or exclusive tax is applied. Item discounts are already incorporated
* `subtotal_excluding_tax` - The integer amount in cents (or local equivalent) representing the subtotal of the invoice before any invoice level discount or tax is applied. Item discounts are already incorporated
* `test_clock` - ID of the test clock this invoice belongs to.
* `threshold_reason` - See [`threshold_reason`](#threshold_reason) below.
* `total` - Total after discounts and taxes.
* `total_discount_amounts` - The aggregate amounts calculated per discount across all line items. See [`total_discount_amounts`](#total_discount_amounts) below.
* `total_excluding_tax` - The integer amount in cents (or local equivalent) representing the total amount of the invoice including all discounts but excluding all tax.
* `total_pretax_credit_amounts` - Contains pretax credit amounts (ex: discount, credit grants, etc) that apply to this invoice. This is a combined list of total_pretax_credit_amounts across all invoice line items. See [`total_pretax_credit_amounts`](#total_pretax_credit_amounts) below.
* `total_taxes` - The aggregate tax information of all line items. See [`total_taxes`](#total_taxes) below.
* `webhooks_delivered_at` - Invoices are automatically paid or sent 1 hour after webhooks are delivered, or until all webhook delivery attempts have [been exhausted](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/webhooks#understand). This field tracks the time when webhooks for this invoice were successfully delivered. If the invoice had no webhooks to deliver, this will be set while the invoice is being created.

<a id="confirmation_secret"></a>
### `confirmation_secret`

The `confirmation_secret` attribute supports:

* `client_secret` - (Sensitive) The client_secret of the payment that Stripe creates for the invoice after finalization.
* `type` - The type of client_secret. Currently this is always payment_intent, referencing the default payment_intent that Stripe creates during invoice finalization

<a id="lines"></a>
### `lines`

The `lines` attribute supports:

* `data` - Details about each object. See [`lines.data`](#lines.data) below.
* `has_more` - True if this list has another page of items after this one that can be fetched.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Always has the value `list`. Possible values: `list`.
* `url` - The URL where this list can be accessed.

<a id="lines.data"></a>
### `lines.data`

The `lines.data` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - The amount, in cents (or local equivalent).
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `description` - An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.
* `discount_amounts` - The amount of discount calculated per discount for this line item. See [`lines.data.discount_amounts`](#lines.data.discount_amounts) below.
* `discountable` - If true, discounts will apply to this line item. Always false for prorations.
* `discounts` - The discounts applied to the invoice line item. Line item discounts are applied before invoice discounts. Use `expand[]=discounts` to expand each discount.
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `invoice` - The ID of the invoice that contains this line item.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Note that for line items with `type=subscription`, `metadata` reflects the current metadata from the subscription associated with the line item, unless the invoice line was directly updated with different metadata after creation.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `line_item`.
* `parent` - The parent that generated this line item. See [`lines.data.parent`](#lines.data.parent) below.
* `period` - See [`lines.data.period`](#lines.data.period) below.
* `pretax_credit_amounts` - Contains pretax credit amounts (ex: discount, credit grants, etc) that apply to this line item. See [`lines.data.pretax_credit_amounts`](#lines.data.pretax_credit_amounts) below.
* `pricing` - The pricing information of the line item. See [`lines.data.pricing`](#lines.data.pricing) below.
* `quantity` - Quantity of units for the invoice line item in integer format, with any decimal precision truncated. For the line item's full-precision decimal quantity, use `quantity_decimal`. This field will be deprecated in favor of `quantity_decimal` in a future version. If the line item is a proration or subscription, the quantity of the subscription that the proration was computed for.
* `quantity_decimal` - Non-negative decimal with at most 12 decimal places. The quantity of units for the line item.
* `subscription` -
* `subtotal` - The subtotal of the line item, in cents (or local equivalent), before any discounts or taxes.
* `taxes` - The tax information of the line item. See [`lines.data.taxes`](#lines.data.taxes) below.

<a id="lines.data.discount_amounts"></a>
### `lines.data.discount_amounts`

The `lines.data.discount_amounts` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - The amount, in cents (or local equivalent), of the discount.
* `discount` - The discount that was applied to get this discount amount.

<a id="lines.data.parent"></a>
### `lines.data.parent`

The `lines.data.parent` attribute supports:

* `invoice_item_details` - Details about the invoice item that generated this line item See [`lines.data.parent.invoice_item_details`](#lines.data.parent.invoice_item_details) below.
* `subscription_item_details` - Details about the subscription item that generated this line item See [`lines.data.parent.subscription_item_details`](#lines.data.parent.subscription_item_details) below.
* `type` - The type of parent that generated this line item Possible values: `invoice_item_details`, `subscription_item_details`.

<a id="lines.data.parent.invoice_item_details"></a>
### `lines.data.parent.invoice_item_details`

The `lines.data.parent.invoice_item_details` attribute supports:

* `invoice_item` - The invoice item that generated this line item
* `proration` - Whether this is a proration
* `proration_details` - Additional details for proration line items See [`lines.data.parent.invoice_item_details.proration_details`](#lines.data.parent.invoice_item_details.proration_details) below.
* `subscription` - The subscription that the invoice item belongs to

<a id="lines.data.parent.invoice_item_details.proration_details"></a>
### `lines.data.parent.invoice_item_details.proration_details`

The `lines.data.parent.invoice_item_details.proration_details` attribute supports:

* `credited_items` - For a credit proration `line_item`, the original debit line_items to which the credit proration applies. See [`lines.data.parent.invoice_item_details.proration_details.credited_items`](#lines.data.parent.invoice_item_details.proration_details.credited_items) below.

<a id="lines.data.parent.invoice_item_details.proration_details.credited_items"></a>
### `lines.data.parent.invoice_item_details.proration_details.credited_items`

The `lines.data.parent.invoice_item_details.proration_details.credited_items` attribute supports:

* `invoice` - Invoice containing the credited invoice line items
* `invoice_line_items` - Credited invoice line items

<a id="lines.data.parent.subscription_item_details"></a>
### `lines.data.parent.subscription_item_details`

The `lines.data.parent.subscription_item_details` attribute supports:

* `invoice_item` - The invoice item that generated this line item
* `proration` - Whether this is a proration
* `proration_details` - Additional details for proration line items See [`lines.data.parent.subscription_item_details.proration_details`](#lines.data.parent.subscription_item_details.proration_details) below.
* `subscription` - The subscription that the subscription item belongs to
* `subscription_item` - The subscription item that generated this line item

<a id="lines.data.parent.subscription_item_details.proration_details"></a>
### `lines.data.parent.subscription_item_details.proration_details`

The `lines.data.parent.subscription_item_details.proration_details` attribute supports:

* `credited_items` - For a credit proration `line_item`, the original debit line_items to which the credit proration applies. See [`lines.data.parent.subscription_item_details.proration_details.credited_items`](#lines.data.parent.subscription_item_details.proration_details.credited_items) below.

<a id="lines.data.parent.subscription_item_details.proration_details.credited_items"></a>
### `lines.data.parent.subscription_item_details.proration_details.credited_items`

The `lines.data.parent.subscription_item_details.proration_details.credited_items` attribute supports:

* `invoice` - Invoice containing the credited invoice line items
* `invoice_line_items` - Credited invoice line items

<a id="lines.data.period"></a>
### `lines.data.period`

The `lines.data.period` attribute supports:

* `end` - The end of the period, which must be greater than or equal to the start. This value is inclusive.
* `start` - The start of the period. This value is inclusive.

<a id="lines.data.pretax_credit_amounts"></a>
### `lines.data.pretax_credit_amounts`

The `lines.data.pretax_credit_amounts` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - The amount, in cents (or local equivalent), of the pretax credit amount.
* `credit_balance_transaction` - The credit balance transaction that was applied to get this pretax credit amount.
* `discount` - The discount that was applied to get this pretax credit amount.
* `type` - Type of the pretax credit amount referenced. Possible values: `credit_balance_transaction`, `discount`.

<a id="lines.data.pricing"></a>
### `lines.data.pricing`

The `lines.data.pricing` attribute supports:

* `price_details` - See [`lines.data.pricing.price_details`](#lines.data.pricing.price_details) below.
* `type` - The type of the pricing details. Possible values: `price_details`.
* `unit_amount_decimal` - The unit amount (in the `currency` specified) of the item which contains a decimal value with at most 12 decimal places.

<a id="lines.data.pricing.price_details"></a>
### `lines.data.pricing.price_details`

The `lines.data.pricing.price_details` attribute supports:

* `price` - The ID of the price this item is associated with.
* `product` - The ID of the product this item is associated with.

<a id="lines.data.taxes"></a>
### `lines.data.taxes`

The `lines.data.taxes` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - The amount of the tax, in cents (or local equivalent).
* `tax_behavior` - Whether this tax is inclusive or exclusive. Possible values: `exclusive`, `inclusive`.
* `tax_rate_details` - Additional details about the tax rate. Only present when `type` is `tax_rate_details`. See [`lines.data.taxes.tax_rate_details`](#lines.data.taxes.tax_rate_details) below.
* `taxability_reason` - The reasoning behind this tax, for example, if the product is tax exempt. The possible values for this field may be extended as new tax rules are supported. Possible values: `customer_exempt`, `not_available`, `not_collecting`, `not_subject_to_tax`, `not_supported`, `portion_product_exempt`, `portion_reduced_rated`, `portion_standard_rated`, `product_exempt`, `product_exempt_holiday`, `proportionally_rated`, `reduced_rated`, `reverse_charge`, `standard_rated`, `taxable_basis_reduced`, `zero_rated`.
* `taxable_amount` - The amount on which tax is calculated, in cents (or local equivalent).
* `type` - The type of tax information. Possible values: `tax_rate_details`.

<a id="lines.data.taxes.tax_rate_details"></a>
### `lines.data.taxes.tax_rate_details`

The `lines.data.taxes.tax_rate_details` attribute supports:

* `tax_rate` - ID of the tax rate

<a id="parent"></a>
### `parent`

The `parent` attribute supports:

* `quote_details` - Details about the quote that generated this invoice See [`parent.quote_details`](#parent.quote_details) below.
* `subscription_details` - Details about the subscription that generated this invoice See [`parent.subscription_details`](#parent.subscription_details) below.
* `type` - The type of parent that generated this invoice Possible values: `quote_details`, `subscription_details`.

<a id="parent.quote_details"></a>
### `parent.quote_details`

The `parent.quote_details` attribute supports:

* `quote` - The quote that generated this invoice

<a id="parent.subscription_details"></a>
### `parent.subscription_details`

The `parent.subscription_details` attribute supports:

* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) defined as subscription metadata when an invoice is created. Becomes an immutable snapshot of the subscription metadata at the time of invoice finalization. *Note: This attribute is populated only for invoices created on or after June 29, 2023.*
* `subscription` - The subscription that generated this invoice
* `subscription_proration_date` - Only set for upcoming invoices that preview prorations. The time used to calculate prorations.

<a id="payments"></a>
### `payments`

The `payments` attribute supports:

* `data` - Details about each object. See [`payments.data`](#payments.data) below.
* `has_more` - True if this list has another page of items after this one that can be fetched.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Always has the value `list`. Possible values: `list`.
* `url` - The URL where this list can be accessed.

<a id="payments.data"></a>
### `payments.data`

The `payments.data` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount_paid` - Amount that was actually paid for this invoice, in cents (or local equivalent). This field is null until the payment is `paid`. This amount can be less than the `amount_requested` if the PaymentIntent’s `amount_received` is not sufficient to pay all of the invoices that it is attached to.
* `amount_requested` - Amount intended to be paid toward this invoice, in cents (or local equivalent)
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `invoice` - The invoice that was paid.
* `is_default` - Stripe automatically creates a default InvoicePayment when the invoice is finalized, and keeps it synchronized with the invoice’s `amount_remaining`. The PaymentIntent associated with the default payment can’t be edited or canceled directly.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `invoice_payment`.
* `payment` - See [`payments.data.payment`](#payments.data.payment) below.
* `status` - The status of the payment, one of `open`, `paid`, or `canceled`.
* `status_transitions` - See [`payments.data.status_transitions`](#payments.data.status_transitions) below.

<a id="payments.data.payment"></a>
### `payments.data.payment`

The `payments.data.payment` attribute supports:

* `charge` - ID of the successful charge for this payment when `type` is `charge`. Note: charge is only surfaced if the charge object is not associated with a payment intent. If the charge object does have a payment intent, the Invoice Payment surfaces the payment intent instead.
* `payment_intent` - ID of the PaymentIntent associated with this payment when `type` is `payment_intent`. Note: This property is only populated for invoices finalized on or after March 15th, 2019.
* `payment_record` - ID of the PaymentRecord associated with this payment when `type` is `payment_record`.
* `type` - Type of payment object associated with this invoice payment. Possible values: `charge`, `payment_intent`, `payment_record`.

<a id="payments.data.status_transitions"></a>
### `payments.data.status_transitions`

The `payments.data.status_transitions` attribute supports:

* `canceled_at` - The time that the payment was canceled.
* `paid_at` - The time that the payment succeeded.

<a id="status_details"></a>
### `status_details`

The `status_details` attribute supports:

* `uncollectible` - See [`status_details.uncollectible`](#status_details.uncollectible) below.

<a id="status_details.uncollectible"></a>
### `status_details.uncollectible`

The `status_details.uncollectible` attribute supports:

* `reason` - The reason why the invoice is uncollectible. Possible values: `max_payment_attempts`, `payment_not_received`, `subscription_canceled`, `subscription_paused`, `user_forgiven`.

<a id="status_transitions"></a>
### `status_transitions`

The `status_transitions` attribute supports:

* `finalized_at` - The time that the invoice draft was finalized.
* `marked_uncollectible_at` - The time that the invoice was marked uncollectible.
* `paid_at` - The time that the invoice was paid.
* `voided_at` - The time that the invoice was voided.

<a id="threshold_reason"></a>
### `threshold_reason`

The `threshold_reason` attribute supports:

* `amount_gte` - The total invoice amount threshold boundary if it triggered the threshold invoice.
* `item_reasons` - Indicates which line items triggered a threshold invoice. See [`threshold_reason.item_reasons`](#threshold_reason.item_reasons) below.

<a id="threshold_reason.item_reasons"></a>
### `threshold_reason.item_reasons`

The `threshold_reason.item_reasons` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `line_item_ids` - The IDs of the line items that triggered the threshold invoice.
* `usage_gte` - The quantity threshold boundary that applied to the given line item.

<a id="total_discount_amounts"></a>

The `total_discount_amounts` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `discount` - The discount that was applied to get this discount amount.

* `taxable_amount` - The amount on which tax is calculated, in cents (or local equivalent).

<a id="total_taxes.tax_rate_details"></a>
### `total_taxes.tax_rate_details`

## Timeouts

[Configuration options](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/syntax#operation-timeouts) are set with the `timeouts` attribute, for example `timeouts = { create = "5m" }`:

* `create` - (Default `20m`)
* `delete` - (Default `20m`)
* `update` - (Default `20m`)

## Removing from State

To stop managing an invoice whose destroy is refused, remove it from the state without destroying it. In Terraform 1.7 and later, and OpenTofu 1.10 and later, replace the `resource` block with a [`removed` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/removed) and apply:

```terraform
removed {
  from = stripe_invoice.setup

  lifecycle {
    destroy = false
  }
}
```

Using `terraform state rm`:

```console
% terraform state rm stripe_invoice.setup
```

The invoice stays in the Stripe account. Replacing one with `terraform apply -replace` or `terraform taint` fails in the same way, at apply.

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import an invoice using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_invoice.setup
  id = "in_123"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_invoice.setup
  identity = {
    id = "in_123"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the invoice.

Using `terraform import`, import an invoice using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_invoice.setup in_123
```

~> Stripe does not return `days_until_due`, `pending_invoice_items_behavior`, `application_fee_amount`, `subscription` or `transfer_data`, so an imported invoice has them null. Leave them out of its configuration: setting one is a change, which Stripe refuses once the invoice is finalized. Stripe does not return `payment_settings.payment_method_options.card.installments.plan` or `shipping_cost.shipping_rate_data`, so an imported invoice has them null: a configuration that sets one plans a replacement after the import.
